# WO-2026-08-12-03 — Close the Keel authority-deviation conflict, without widening it into a hole

## Acceptance criteria

**The conflict, stated once.** Keel's contract makes any `credential_scope` or `live_authority` other than
`none` **a refusal condition in itself**. The estate's own canonical Work Order template defines those as
**standing DEFAULTS with an explicit deviation mechanism**, and `tools/wo/envelope.mjs` emits deviations
with a mandatory `--deviation-authority`. **The contract forbids what the tooling is built to express.**
It has now blocked two consecutive correctly-formed Work Orders (WO-2026-08-12-01-v2 and -02), each time
resolved only by Larry invoking CLAUDE.md precedence in the order body. That is a workaround, not a fix.

**AC1 — diagnose before drafting.** Establish by reading, and state in your return: every site in Keel's
contract that derives behaviour from `credential_scope`/`live_authority`, and for each, whether it states
**(a)** the standing default, **(b)** a refusal trigger, or **(c)** a genuine safety behaviour that must
survive untouched. Larry's read found sites at ~121-123, ~301, ~312, ~401 and ~623-624 — **treat that as a
starting point, not the answer, and correct it if it is wrong.**
⚠️ **Line ~401's "credential_scope: none is absolute" is a DIFFERENT proposition** — it forbids harvesting
other sessions' credentials (including `~/.codex/*`). **That must remain absolute.** Do not collapse it
into the standing-default clause.

**AC2 — produce an EXACT redline BEFORE applying it.** CLAUDE.md § "No silent constitutional
self-modification" requires it. Write the before/after of every changed passage to
`Deliverables/2026-08-12-nolan-keel-credential-scope-contract-redline.md`, then apply. The redline document
is the artefact an independent reviewer reads; it must stand alone without the diff.

**AC3 — ⛔ THE SAFETY PROPERTY. Read this before writing a word; it is the whole difficulty of the order.**
The amendment must permit a **BOUNDED, DECLARED, EXTERNALLY-AUTHORISED** deviation — one written into the
order's frontmatter, naming its scope, with a `deviation_authority` naming who authorised it and when.
It must **still REFUSE**:
- a credential scope the worker **assumes, infers or grants itself**;
- a deviation with **no named authority**;
- a deviation whose scope is **vague or unbounded** ("as needed", "full access");
- anything that would let a worker **read another session's credentials** (AC1's site ~401, untouched).

**A widening that loses those is a WORSE outcome than the conflict it replaces.** If you cannot draft
wording that holds both halves, say so and return — do not ship a loosened contract.

**AC4 — internal consistency across BOTH sites.** The standing-default clause and the REFUSED verdict
definition must agree after the change. **v1 of this problem is that they were consistent with each other
and inconsistent with the estate; do not fix one and leave the other**, which would make Keel's contract
self-contradictory — strictly worse than today.

**AC5 — REPORT, do not fix: your own contract does not grant contract amendment.** `Team/Nolan - HR/AGENTS.md`
covers hiring — authoring a NEW specialist's contract via SOP-001. It has no clause about amending an
existing one, yet Keel's contract names you as the amender. **Recommend how that should be closed; do NOT
apply it to your own contract.** Warwick approved fixing the KEEL conflict, not a Nolan self-amendment,
and self-modification on relayed authority is exactly what CLAUDE.md prohibits.

**AC6 — prove the amendment against the two live cases, by reading.** Take the already-issued
`Deliverables/2026-08-12-wo-b15-30-region-granularity-and-measurement.md` (four BOUNDED deviations, named
authority) and state what a fresh Keel reading ONLY the amended contract would verdict on the authority
question — it must be ACCEPT. Then construct a **counter-case**: the same order with the deviation authority
stripped. It must still be REFUSE. **Both, or the amendment failed.**

# ⚑ AMENDMENT 1 — Larry, 2026-08-12, after Nolan's CLARIFY read-back

**OPERATIVE. Supersedes anything above it that it contradicts.** Both blockers resolved; every observation
answered. Per `CLAUDE.md` this earns ONE further read-back — keep it short, then proceed.

## C1 / M1 — UPHELD. **Take option (B). Critical rule 3 is reconciled in the same commit.**

**Nolan is right and the order was wrong.** Critical rule 3 (~L382) — *"NEVER touch a live service,
scheduled task, or non-throwaway database"* — is an **independent absolute**, and WO-2026-08-12-02's own
bounded deviation grants SELECT-only reads of `asdair.regulars`, **a live non-throwaway database**. A fresh
Keel reading only the two sites I named could still refuse that order on critical rule 3 alone. **My AC6
wording — "on the authority question alone" — masked exactly that rather than resolving it. That was a
defect in the order, not a subtlety.**

**Option (A) is rejected**: it leaves the conflict to recur on the next live-execution order, which is the
recurrence this whole Work Order exists to end.

**AUTHORISED — option (B), with Nolan's proposed shape, which is correct:** critical rule 3 binds absolutely
under the standing default and is displaced **only to the exact extent of a valid, bounded `live_authority`
deviation naming the target and the permitted operations.**

**⛔ NEVER reachable by ANY deviation — this list is the safety property and must appear in the contract
text itself, not merely in this order:**
- a **migration or DDL** against a non-disposable database;
- **any write to live data** (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE);
- **operating or supervising a live service** — start, stop, restart, deregister.

That matches what WO-02's deviation already said of itself (*"SELECT-ONLY, NO INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or
DDL"*) and keeps L311–313 true. **Larry's reasoning, recorded as Larry's:** this is the same
contract-versus-estate drift, not a new widening — the estate has been issuing bounded live-read deviations
and resolving them by precedence in the order body. **The purpose is to make the contract state the limits
that are already being applied, and to make anything outside them impossible to reach.** If drafting reveals
that (B) cannot be written without loosening one of the three never-reachable items, **stop and return that
finding** — do not ship it.
